Description:
Details of Incident:

It was observed that Ms. Shane Lerado failed to comply with the company's attendance and sick leave notification policy. The employee informed management of her intended absence at 11:42 PM, which did not meet the required notification timeline.

Per company policy, employees are required to notify management and/or call the designated sick hotline at least two (2) hours prior to the start of their scheduled shift when taking a sick leave. This procedure is in place to allow sufficient time for operational planning and to arrange coverage for the employee's scheduled duties.

In this instance, Ms. Lerado:

Failed to provide the required two-hour advance notice before the start of her scheduled shift.
Failed to call or notify the designated sick hotline as required by company guidelines.
Did not follow the established attendance procedures, which impacted the team's ability to secure coverage for her absence and maintain operational efficiency.

This late notice will already cause an impact with the operation, which agent is already informed about the proper guidelines.

We recommend issuing a Written Warning as the advisor demonstrated poor active listening and communication skills during the interaction. The advisor interrupted the customer, failed to acknowledge the customer's comments and concerns, and did not consistently use proper phone etiquette.

Please see the attached file for the incident date. Thank you.
Employee Explanation:
I am writing to express my commitment to improving my active listening skills when interacting with customers. I understand that effective communication is very important to provide excellent customer service, building trust, and ensuring customer satisfaction.

To enhance my active listening abilities, I will focus on giving customers my full attention, avoiding interruptions, and carefully understanding their concerns before responding. I will also practice asking clarifying questions, paraphrasing key points to confirm understanding, and demonstrating empathy toward each customer's situation.

By improving these skills, I aim to provide more accurate solutions, reduce misunderstandings, and create a positive experience for every customer. I believe that strengthening my active listening will contribute to better customer relationships and support the overall goals of our organization.

Thank you for your guidance and support as I continue to develop professionally. I am committed to applying these improvements consistently in my daily interactions with customers.

Employee Explanation:
As an Operations Manager, I take full responsibility for ensuring the accuracy and integrity of all data presented during our Weekly Business Reviews (WBR). While there was an oversight regarding the data provided by the WFM team in our recent WBR, we chose to address the matter offline. It was important to me that we handle this professionally and maintain a unified front as a team, rather than singling anyone out during the presentation.

To prevent this from happening again and to ensure smoother operations across the board, I have outlined the following action plan moving forward:

Enhanced Internal Dry Runs: We will implement a stricter validation process during our internal WBR dry runs. Every piece of data will be thoroughly double-checked before the actual client presentation.

Comprehensive Training for Connie (Interim AM, AIFI): I will be working closely with Connie to calibrate her skills in data analysis. We will focus on data mining, accurate interpretation, and cross-referencing figures using the latest raw data. It is a top priority that she fully understands how our KPIs are calculated and the specific drivers needed to achieve our targets.

Client-Facing Development: It is my responsibility to help Connie build her confidence in client interactions. I will be coaching her extensively on active listening and effective communication so that she feels comfortable and prepared to address client questions without feeling overwhelmed as she immerses herself in this role.

Daily Data Visibility: A key challenge we faced was the lack of daily raw data updates from WFM, which restricted Connie and our Team Leads from having real-time visibility into daily operator performance. We are now closely coordinating with WFM to ensure data is updated daily. This will empower the leadership team to immediately identify and address any sudden fluctuations in our KPIs.

Moving forward, we are committed to fostering a strong, seamless collaboration between the Operations, WFM, and TQA teams to drive operational excellence.

Description: A violation in the Code of Discipline Group II Provisions on Performance of Duties 2.20 Failure to Meet Client Targets and 4.89 - Gross/Reckless Negligence in the performance of the assigned duties dated June 25, 2026 where in the during the Weekly Business Review under your management has incurred incorrect data presented resulted to client frustrations and reflecting mismanagement.
Employee Explanation:
I would like to formally respond to the allegation of Gross/Reckless Negligence in the performance of my assigned duties during the Weekly Business Review (WBR) conducted on June 25, 2026.

Upon review of the incident, I acknowledge that incorrect data was presented during the WBR, which resulted in confusion, client frustration, and reflected poorly on the management of the account. The data provided by Workforce Management (WFM) was inadvertently presented as the combined AHT instead of the AHT without Planogram annotation. Unfortunately, I failed to thoroughly validate the figures prior to the presentation.

I take full accountability for this oversight. I became complacent in my review process as the chart had already been prepared and pasted into the presentation. My focus was primarily on verifying the current week's data, and I neglected to thoroughly review and validate the previous week's figures and the methodology used in the computation. This lapse in diligence led to the inaccurate presentation of data.

I recognize that as the person accountable for the account, it is my responsibility to ensure that all information presented to clients is accurate, validated, and properly reviewed before any business presentation. Regardless of the source of the data, the responsibility ultimately rests with me.

Moving forward, I will implement stricter validation procedures prior to all business reviews, including cross-checking all metrics, verifying data sources, and conducting a comprehensive review of both current and historical figures before presentation. This will help ensure the accuracy and integrity of the information being communicated to our clients and prevent similar incidents from occurring in the future.

I sincerely apologize for this mistake and any inconvenience or concern it may have caused. I am committed to learning from this experience and strengthening my review processes to uphold the standards expected of my role.

On the scheduled workday immediately following payday, which is considered a Critical Workday, Ms. Shane Lerado failed to report for her scheduled shift, resulting in an unauthorized absence.

Prior to the start of her shift, Ms. Lerado informed her Team Leaders at exactly 11:38PM, that she had traveled to Balamban, her hometown, and stated that she would try her best to report for a half-day shift. Based on this information, she was expected to provide updates regarding her availability. However, no further communication or status update was received throughout the shift. Despite waiting for an update, Ms. Lerado did not report to work and did not notify management that she would no longer be able to fulfill her commitment.

During the discussion, it was emphasized that personal activities such as traveling to her hometown should be planned in a way that does not compromise scheduled workdays, particularly on a Critical Workday. Since her schedule is 12:00 AM to 8:00 AM, she had several alternatives available, such as:

Scheduling her trip on her rest day.
Traveling after completing her scheduled shift.
Making appropriate arrangements in advance if she anticipated that reporting to work would not be possible.

These options could have prevented the disruption to operations and avoided an unauthorized absence.

Ms. Lerado was reminded of the importance of adhering to the company's attendance policy, especially during Critical Work Days, and of maintaining timely communication with management whenever unforeseen circumstances arise. Employees are expected to provide prompt updates if there are changes to their ability to report for work, rather than leaving the status uncertain.

Based on the circumstances and the attendance policy, this incident is being documented under Violation 1.31 – Absence during a Critical Workday, as the employee incurred an unauthorized absence on a designated Critical Workday following payday.

On June 20, 2026, Shane Lerado was reminded of the company's attendance policy, specifically the requirement to notify the company or call the sick hotline at least two (2) hours before the start of the scheduled shift if she would be absent due to illness etc. The expectation and procedure were clearly communicated to avoid operational disruption.

Shane is expected to strictly comply with the company's attendance and notification procedures moving forward to prevent further disciplinary action.

Description:
Based on the performance evaluation conducted, Keith Rocero has consistently failed to meet the client's quality target due to recurring quality errors across multiple audit periods.

From Week 19 to Week 22, Keith incurred multiple quality errors, indicating a pattern of non-compliance with the required quality standards. Although she successfully passed Week 23 without any recorded errors, the improvement was not sustained. She again incurred quality errors in Week 24, and in Week 25, she incurred two (2) quality errors within a single session, further demonstrating a recurring performance issue.

Throughout this period, multiple corrective measures were implemented, including coaching sessions, performance discussions, corrective action plans, and continuous monitoring. Despite these interventions, there has been no significant or sustained improvement in her overall performance.

It was also noted that several corrective action acknowledgments were not completed by Keith. During the discussion, she explained that the notification emails were automatically routed to her spam folder and that she did not regularly check her spam messages. While this explains the missed acknowledgments, employees are expected to regularly monitor their company email, including spam folders when necessary, to ensure timely receipt of important communications and compliance with company directives.

Considering the recurring quality issues, the lack of sustained improvement despite repeated coaching and corrective actions, and the continued failure to consistently meet the client's quality expectations, it is evident that the interventions provided have not resulted in the required performance improvement.
Employee Explanation:

To be honest, I regularly check my email. However, no one informed me that there was a corrective action form that I needed to sign and acknowledge. During the coaching sessions regarding my errors over the past few weeks, the Team Leaders who handled my coaching only instructed me to acknowledge my coaching logs. Because of this, I genuinely had no idea that there was a separate corrective action form that required my acknowledgment.

It was only when AM Connie Jimenez informed me about it on Monday, June 29, 2026, at 9:24 PM, that I became aware of the requirement. As soon as I understood the situation, I realized my mistake.

The agent openly shared the reason for the unauthorized absence. He explained that their family had a gathering and initially informed his Team Leader that he might only be late for his scheduled shift. However, he was ultimately unable to report to work.

During the coaching discussion, I asked the agent to elaborate on the underlying reason for his absence. He shared that following the passing of his father last month, he has been experiencing frequent overthinking, particularly regarding his mother's health and well-being. He admitted that these thoughts have been emotionally overwhelming, and in an attempt to temporarily cope with the stress, he consumed alcoholic beverages. The agent also mentioned that he had already prepared himself for work and intended to report for his shift, but due to his condition, he was unable to do so.

LEADER'S SIDE:

I conducted a coaching session with the agent regarding the importance of maintaining good attendance and fulfilling work schedule commitments. I also reviewed the company's Code of Conduct and Discipline Refresher, specifically discussing the policy on unauthorized absences and the potential consequences of attendance violations.

I acknowledged the personal challenges the agent is currently experiencing while reinforcing that, regardless of personal circumstances, it remains every employee's responsibility to report for work as scheduled or follow the proper call-out and notification process whenever attendance issues arise. I encouraged the agent to communicate proactively should personal concerns affect his ability to report to work in the future so that appropriate support and guidance can be provided.

ACTION PLAN:
The agent will strictly comply with the company attendance policy and report to work according to his assigned schedule.
If unforeseen personal circumstances arise, the agent will immediately notify his Team Leader through the proper communication channels before the start of his shift.
The agent will avoid engaging in activities that may prevent him from reporting to work as scheduled, particularly before workdays.
The Team Leader will continue to monitor the agent's attendance and conduct regular follow-up coaching sessions to provide guidance and ensure sustained improvement.
AGENT'S COMMITMENT:

"I understand that my absence was my responsibility, regardless of my personal situation. Moving forward, I will manage my personal concerns more responsibly, strictly follow the attendance policy, communicate immediately if issues arise, and ensure that I report to work as scheduled. I am committed to improving my attendance and maintaining my accountability as a member of the team."

I understand that my personal circumstances do not excuse my failure to report to work, and I take full responsibility for my actions. I recognize the importance of maintaining attendance, communicating effectively, and fulfilling my responsibilities as a member of the team. I sincerely apologize for my absence and for any inconvenience it may have caused.

I am committed to strictly complying with the company's attendance and punctuality policies and will ensure that I report to work as scheduled. I will practice healthier ways of coping with stress and grief instead of making decisions that could negatively impact my work responsibilities, and I will avoid consuming alcohol before a scheduled shift or in any situation that may prevent me from reporting to work. I will also strive to maintain a healthy balance between my personal responsibilities and work commitments by seeking support from my family or available employee resources whenever needed. I understand that my attendance is my responsibility, and I am committed to learning from this experience by remaining accountable, communicating proactively, maintaining consistent attendance, and continuously improving my reliability and performance as a dependable member of the team.

I sincerely acknowledge the importance of taking full responsibility for my attendance and actions as an agent. Moving forward, I commit to being more accountable, responsible, and consistent in fulfilling my work obligations.

I will make every effort to report to work on time and as scheduled, and I will proactively communicate with my Team Leader should I encounter any personal, family, or emergency situation that may affect my attendance. I understand that timely and proper communication is essential to minimize the impact on the team and business operations.

I also commit to handling personal challenges and emotional difficulties in a healthier and more appropriate manner. I will seek support when necessary and ensure that personal circumstances do not affect my ability to perform my responsibilities professionally. I will avoid making decisions that could compromise my attendance, judgment, or performance.

I understand the seriousness of this matter and the trust placed in me as an agent. I take this experience as an opportunity to learn and improve. Moving forward, I will demonstrate greater discipline, reliability, accountability, and professionalism. I am committed to maintaining consistent attendance, following company policies and procedures, and becoming a more dependable member of the team.

I conducted a discussion with QA Juvelyn Siaboc and Roanne Malinis regarding their leave request for July 1, 2026. During our conversation, I acknowledged that their leave request had already been approved by their immediate supervisor from TOG. However, I explained that, in accordance with Empire One's leave policy, all leave requests must also be processed and approved internally. I further clarified that leave applications are expected to be submitted at least one to two weeks in advance and remain subject to approval based on business and operational requirements.

While I was explaining the policy and the reason why the request could not be immediately accommodated, Roanne Malinis abruptly left the discussion before I had finished providing the necessary information and before the meeting was formally concluded. She did not allow me to complete the discussion or acknowledge the instructions that were being communicated.
After leaving the discussion, Roanne expressed at her workstation that she would still proceed with her absence if her leave request was not accommodated. This statement was made despite the explanation provided regarding the company's leave approval process and policy requirements.
By walking out of the discussion before it was concluded and indicating an intention to disregard the established leave approval process, Roanne failed to comply with a reasonable management directive and demonstrated behavior inconsistent with the company's policies and expected standards of professionalism.
Employee Explanation:
To the Management,

I respectfully submit my response regarding the discussion held concerning my leave request for July 1, 2026.

First, I would like to clarify that my leave request was submitted and approved by my immediate supervisor from TOG. At the time, I understood that the approval provided was sufficient and was not fully aware that an additional internal approval process was still required under Empire One's leave policy. I acknowledge the importance of complying with all company procedures and appreciate the clarification that was provided during the discussion.

Regarding the meeting, it was never my intention to be disrespectful, disregard management instructions, or disrupt the discussion. If my departure before the meeting formally concluded was interpreted as unprofessional or dismissive, I sincerely apologize. My actions were not meant to prevent the completion of the discussion nor to show disrespect toward the individuals involved.

I would also like to clarify that any statements I made concerning my planned absence were made out of concern regarding prior personal commitments that had already been arranged based on my understanding that my leave had been approved. Description:
OVERSTAFFING
On July 10, 2026 (MNL), TL Daryl was unable to perform the required staffing verification prior to the start of operations due to circumstances on his end. Instead of validating the staffing requirement through the established Operations process, he sought confirmation from Ben Balocos, who is currently aligned with the Training and Quality team and is not responsible for daily staffing management.

At the time, operator Rechelle Bantillo was absent. However, based on the approved staffing plan for the shift, the team already had one (1) available buffer, which was sufficient to absorb the absence without requiring additional staffing coverage. During Daryl's discussion with Ben, he asked whether all operators would be processing. Ben confirmed that everyone would be processing, taking into consideration the reported absence. Because Ben was not directly managing the daily staffing plan, he was unaware that a staffing buffer had already been allocated.

Relying on this information, Daryl assumed that Rechelle Bantillo's credentials needed to be covered. Without independently verifying the staffing requirement against the official staffing plan or coordinating with the Operations team, he proceeded to assign an additional operator to process using Rechelle's credentials.

As a result, the team became overstaffed for approximately two (2) hours. The incident was primarily caused by the failure to verify staffing requirements through the appropriate operational process and the reliance on information from a resource who was not responsible for daily staffing decisions. Proper validation of the staffing plan before assigning coverage would have prevented the unnecessary overstaffing and ensured efficient utilization of available resources.
Employee Explanation:
Good day,

I would like to respectfully submit my response regarding the Notice to Explain (NTE) issued to me.

First, I would like to clarify that I am uncertain why this incident was classified under Performance of Duties, as I believe the circumstances presented in the NTE do not fully reflect what actually happened.

On July 10, 2026, I arrived at approximately 12:55 AM, five (5) minutes before the start of my scheduled shift. As part of my normal routine, I immediately pulled up my tools to check staffing and attendance. However, I encountered a technical issue that prevented me from accessing the Team Leads' staffing file, making it impossible for me to verify the approved staffing plan at that time.

Before operations started, TL Steph also informed me that Rechelle Bantillo would be absent and instructed me to ensure that her account would be covered. At that point, neither of us was aware that there was already an available staffing buffer for the shift.

Since I could not access the staffing file and needed to ensure that Rechelle Bantillo's account would be logged in on time, I took the initiative to seek confirmation. Because TL Jham was seated far from my station and time was critical, I requested QA Ben to verify with her whether everyone should be logged in.

QA Ben relayed TL Jham's response, which was "Login tanan." Based on that information, I understood that all operators, including the coverage for Rechelle Bantillo, should proceed with processing. Acting in good faith and with the intention of ensuring uninterrupted operations, I logged in and began processing sessions.

Approximately two (2) hours later, TL Jham asked why I was taking sessions. I explained that I was covering for Rechelle Bantillo. It was only then that I was informed that there was already an available staffing buffer and that additional coverage was not necessary. As soon as this was clarified, I immediately logged out and the existing buffer was utilized.

I would also like to emphasize that I already discussed these details during my coaching session with AM Connie. Despite providing this explanation, a corrective action was still issued.

With this, I respectfully request that the following points be considered:

My actions were made in good faith and were intended to ensure operational continuity while I was unable to access the staffing file due to a technical issue.
I made an effort to verify the situation by requesting confirmation before proceeding. The misunderstanding resulted from the information relayed to me, not from any intentional disregard of process.
Once I became aware that a staffing buffer existed, I immediately corrected the situation by logging out.
To my knowledge, the incident did not result in any significant operational disruption or material impact.
Considering the circumstances, I respectfully believe that classifying this incident as a Performance of Duties issue and issuing a corrective action may not be proportionate to what actually occurred.

I am also concerned that the NTE was sent to my previous company email address. Had I not discovered it, I could have unintentionally failed to respond, which, according to the notice, could have resulted in further disciplinary action up to and including termination. I respectfully request that future notices be sent to my active company email to ensure timely receipt and response.

In view of the facts stated above, I respectfully request that Management reconsider and withdraw the corrective action. I have always performed my duties with the best intentions and remained committed to supporting operations. Receiving a corrective action under these circumstances has been discouraging, especially since I believe I acted responsibly based on the information available to me at that time.

Thank you for your time and consideration. I respectfully ask for a fair and objective review of this matter.

At the time, he was at his grandfather’s house to assist in looking after him due to his grandfather’s condition following a mild stroke. Mr. Laguda was expected to report before 8:00 PM, and his aunt was supposed to cover his time in attending to their grandfather during his scheduled shift. However, due to the circumstances encountered that day, he was unable to report to work on time.

Team Leader Floramae then reiterated the instruction by stating, "Won't you listen to me? I'm a Team Leader here." Ms. Desucatan allegedly replied, "You're not sure. You're not confirmed yet," in reference to Team Leader Floramae's authority.

The exchange occurred on the production floor in the presence of other employees. The incident was witnessed by Team Leader Juverlyn Ortegas and Team Leader Gerald Altizo.

This incident is being reviewed as a possible violation of Section 4.71 of the Company's Code of Conduct, which pertains to Uttering words, committing acts, or making gestures that are manifestly insulting or grossly disrespectful to any employee.
Employee Explanation:
Good day, 

I respectfully submit this response to provide my perspective regarding the incident that led to the corrective action.

At the time of the incident, I had just returned from my break. The Team Lead had arrived early for her shift but, to my knowledge, had not yet officially clocked in. After returning, I was having a normal conversation with my colleague. We were not speaking loudly, and I was surprised when the Team Lead suddenly stood up, called me by my name, and said, "Marvic, you're too loud," in a manner that I perceived as unprofessional.

Because I was caught off guard by the way I was approached, I reacted emotionally and mirrored the same tone. I acknowledge that I made inappropriate remarks during the exchange, and I take responsibility for my part in that. Looking back, I recognize that I could have handled the situation more appropriately despite being surprised.

However, I would also like my concerns to be considered. I believe the situation could have been handled in a more professional and respectful manner. If I needed to be reminded about the noise level, I would have appreciated being approached calmly and respectfully, as I have experienced with other Team Leads. I felt that the interaction became unnecessarily confrontational from the beginning.

I would also like to clarify that the louder conversation and laughter were coming from other agents seated on my side. Those agents themselves acknowledged that they were the ones being loud. In addition, the colleague I was speaking with can confirm that our conversation was at a normal volume.
When I pointed out that other individuals were making more noise, the discussion escalated. During the exchange, the Team Lead responded by saying that she was the "Team Leader." I interpreted this as emphasizing her authority during the disagreement, which contributed to the tension. In response, I stated that she was not yet officially a Team Lead yet. While I regret making that comment, it was a reaction to how the conversation unfolded rather than an attempt to be disrespectful.

There were also other employees in the area who were speaking more loudly but were not addressed. Since I had only just returned from my break, I felt that I was singled out. I respectfully believe that if the concern was about maintaining a quiet work environment, the same standard should have been applied consistently to everyone in the area.

I also believe that leadership comes with the responsibility to communicate professionally and respectfully, especially when addressing employees regarding workplace concerns. I fully accept responsibility for my own reaction, but I also hope that the manner in which I was approached will be taken into consideration.

Lastly, I respectfully request that this matter not be viewed from only one perspective. While I understand that the Team Lead has a witness, there are also several individuals who witnessed the incident from my side and can provide additional context regarding what occurred before and during the interaction. I respectfully ask that their statements also be considered so that a complete and balanced assessment can be made.

In addition, I intend to submit a separate Incident Report regarding the Team Lead's conduct during this interaction. This is not intended as retaliation or to avoid accountability. Rather, I believe it is appropriate for my concerns about how I was approached and how the situation was handled to be formally documented and reviewed. I respectfully request that both my Incident Report and this response be considered together so that management can evaluate the matter fairly and objectively from both perspectives.

My intention is not to avoid accountability. I accept responsibility for my own words and reactions. However, I respectfully ask that my side of the incident also be heard so that a fair and objective decision can be made based on all of the facts. I believe that considering both accounts, along with the statements of all available witnesses, will help ensure that the outcome is impartial and based on the complete circumstances of the incident.


I would like to clarify what happened during the incident. At the time, I was performing my duties as an agent . When my name was mentioned as though I was the one making the noise, I responded because I wanted to defend myself against an accusation that I believed was inaccurate.
My response was not intended to be disrespectful or to challenge your authority. I was simply trying to correct what I believed was a misunderstanding and protect my reputation.

I respect the responsibilities that come with your role as a team leader. At the same time, I hope that in the future, concerns involving team members will be addressed after confirming the facts, and that individuals will be given an opportunity to explain before being identified or accused publicly. I believe this approach helps maintain professionalism, fairness, and mutual respect within the team.
Employee Commitment: I acknowledge the Final Written Warning issued to me and take full responsibility for the matter that led to this sanction. I understand the importance of following company policies, meeting expectations, and maintaining professionalism at all times. Moving forward, I am committed to learning from this experience, improving my actions and decision-making, and ensuring that the same situation will not happen again. I will be more mindful, accountable, and consistent in fulfilling my responsibilities, and I will actively seek guidance whenever necessary. I value my role and the trust given to me, and I am committed to demonstrating positive and sustainable improvement moving forward.

Relying on a coworker to communicate an absence does not satisfy the company's attendance and notification requirements and may result in incomplete or delayed information, making it difficult for management to make timely operational decisions.

The absence occurred during a critical business period, when adequate staffing was essential to maintain productivity, customer service, and operational efficiency. Because no advance notice was provided directly by Gabriel, the team was unable to make timely staffing adjustments, resulting in increased workload for other employees, disruption to workflow, and challenges in meeting operational requirements.

Employees are expected to comply with the company's attendance and notification policy by informing their immediate supervisor as soon as they become aware that they will be unable to report for work. Gabriel's failure to personally communicate his absence constitutes a No Call, No Show (NCNS) incident and is a violation of the company's attendance and communication policy. Employees are accountable for directly communicating attendance concerns and should not rely on teammates to fulfill this responsibility on their behalf.

This matter was discussed with Gabriel during the coaching session, where the expectations regarding attendance and timely communication were reiterated. He was informed that the incident would result in a Corrective Action in accordance with company policy and that future occurrences of similar behavior may lead to further disciplinary action.

On August 10, 2026, an incident involving prolonged non-dialing activity was observed concerning John Ron Pelotinia. The agent was scheduled for a break from 1:00 AM to 1:30 AM. During the shift, I received a notification from QA John Carl advising that John Ron was not actively on the phone.

At the time I received the notification, I was on my scheduled lunch break. I attempted to contact John Ron to determine the reason for the observed inactivity and to verify whether there was any operational or technical concern affecting his availability.

At approximately 2:25 AM, I returned to the production floor to personally verify John Ron's status. Upon checking his workstation, I observed John Ron near his station engaged in conversation with other agents rather than actively taking or placing calls.

A 1-on-1 coaching session has been completed with John Ron Pelotinia. During the coaching, the importance of adherence to scheduled breaks, active-time expectations, and immediately reporting any operational or technical concerns was reinforced.

Given the impact of the incident on team productivity and client operations, a Corrective Action will be filed and documented for proper accountability and follow-through.
Employee Explanation:
Dear Leadership and HR Department,

I am writing this response to the Notice to Explain (NTE) issued on September 18, 2026, concerning the alleged Abandonment of Post and Prolonged Break under the Code of Conduct (COCD) for an incident dated August 12, 2026.

I welcome this opportunity to present my side of the situation and clarify the circumstances surrounding these allegations.

1. Explanation Regarding Unscheduled Break / Offline Status
Original Scheduled Break: 1:00 AM PHT – 1:30 AM PHT

Actual Break Taken: 1:43 AM PHT – 2:13 AM PHT

The allegation that I abandoned my post stems from taking my break outside my scheduled window. However, this was done in direct reliance on instructions cascaded by Ms. Anamie Ababa from the WFM RTA Department.

WFM explicitly informed us that if we miss or delay our scheduled break due to a long call, we must still utilize our full break allowance, as commitment adherence points are already deducted the moment the original slot passes. Relying on this directive, I proceeded to take my entitled 30-minute break starting at 1:43 AM PHT immediately after my call ended.

Furthermore, because our system lacks an option to set our status to "Break" during scheduled phone hours, setting my status to "Offline" was the only available method to step away for my break.

Mitigating Factor / Admission:

I acknowledge that I failed to notify my Team Lead before taking the delayed break. I operated under the assumption that because this rule came directly from WFM RTA, the schedule variance would automatically be understood and reflected. I recognize this gap in communication on my part and will ensure leadership is directly informed of any future break adjustments.

2. Explanation Regarding Alleged Prolonged Break (2:13 AM PHT – 2:25 AM PHT)
I returned to the production floor at 2:13 AM PHT, marking the exact end of my 30-minute break. I did not prolong my personal break.

Upon returning to my station, newly hired agents Euclid Batarilan and Lester Canillo (formerly from the Agero account), who were sitting next to me, approached me to ask for guidance and account insights. Unbeknownst to me at the time, they were actually on their scheduled break. Because floor support leads (Mike Mamac and John Carl) were occupied or unable to assist with their concerns at that moment, I willingly shared my knowledge to support them.

It was during this interaction—while I was answering their questions at my station—that leadership observed us, leading to the perception of a prolonged break. While my intention was purely to help new team members get acclimated, I now realize that engaging with colleagues without verifying their break status or obtaining lead approval created confusion regarding my activity.

3. Operational Concerns: Delayed Issuance & Due Process
While I respect the administrative process, I would like to respectfully express my concern regarding the timeline of this notice:

Incident Date: August 12, 2026

Date NTE Shared/Signed by HR/Leadership: September 18, 2026

Receiving an incident report more than a month after the alleged violation hinders real-time review, impacts accurate memory recall, and delays timely resolution. I respectfully request clarification on why this report was cascaded after a 37-day delay.

CONCLUSION AND COMMITMENTS
To summarize:

Abandonment of Post: I did not abandon my post; I utilized my delayed break allowance per WFM RTA guidelines following a long call, using "Offline" status as it was the only available option.

Prolonged Break: My break ended on time at 2:13 AM PHT. The time until 2:25 AM PHT was spent assisting new colleagues at my station, unaware that they were on break at the time.

Corrective Action: Moving forward, I commit to informing my direct Team Lead whenever a long call delays my break and will direct colleagues seeking help straight to assigned floor support leads.

Thank you for reviewing my explanation. I remain committed to maintaining policy compliance and am open to discussing this matter further if needed.

Attendance and Failure to Provide Medical Certificate

On August 12, 2026, the agent informed the leader in advance that she would be unable to report for work due to a reported health-related concern. The agent was advised to secure and submit a valid medical certificate upon her return to work to support and validate her illness-related absence. The agent acknowledged the instruction and agreed to provide the required documentation.

August 12, 2026 was a scheduled working day for the agent, while August 13, 2026 was her scheduled day off. Considering that the absence was reported to be health-related, consideration was given to the situation; however, the agent was clearly reminded that submission of a valid medical certificate remained a requirement for documentation of the absence.

On August 14, 2026, the agent informed the leader that she was still not feeling well and would again be unable to report for work. The agent was once again reminded to secure and submit the required medical certificate to support her illness-related absences.

On August 15, 2026, the agent returned to work. During the Welcome Back Coaching, the leader requested the required medical certificate. However, the agent was unable to present or submit a valid medical certificate at that time.

In accordance with the COCD Provision on Attendance, Section 1.22, the agent was provided an additional 24-hour period to secure and submit a valid medical certificate together with the required supporting documentation. The agent was clearly informed that failure to submit the required documentation within the prescribed timeframe could result in corrective action.

After the additional 24-hour period, the agent still failed to provide a valid medical certificate. The agent subsequently informed the leader that she went to San Carlos Doctor's Hospital after her shift at approximately 10:00 AM to obtain the required documentation. However, according to the agent, she was unable to secure the certificate because the concerned office was no longer accepting requests due to the cutoff time.

The agent was reminded that the required medical certificate had already been communicated as a condition for supporting and validating her illness-related absences and that an additional 24-hour period had been provided for compliance. The agent acknowledged the situation and stated that she understood the consequences of failing to submit the required documentation.

Despite the initial reminders, repeated follow-up, and additional 24-hour opportunity provided to comply, the agent failed to submit a valid medical certificate to support her illness-related absences. This constitutes non-compliance with the applicable attendance and documentation requirements under COCD Provision on Attendance, Section 1.22, and is being formally documented for appropriate corrective action.
Employee Explanation:
August 12, I failed to report to work due to the difficulties I was experiencing on the 9th day of transitioning from a night shift to a morning shift. As I tried to adjust my body clock during this transition period, I had been going to work for more than five days with only 1–2 hours of sleep, and there was even one occasion when I did not get any sleep at all.

At the same time, I also have part-time jobs, and there was also a day that we experienced power outage in our area. Since the electricity was out only in our village, it became difficult for me to get enough rest during those consecutive days. This was further affected by my irregular eating schedule, as I sometimes only eat one meal a day or eat very late.

Due to these circumstances, my body eventually began to show signs of exhaustion and fatigue. In the days leading up to the second week of August, I continued going to work despite having very little energy, constant headaches, and chills, which also began to affect my work performance.

On the evening of August 11, I was already feeling extremely unwell. I had no energy to eat or even get out of bed, so I had to sleep and rest. When midnight of August 12 came, I informed my Team Leader that I could not afford to go to work because of my condition.

From August 12 to 14, I continued to feel unwell and tried to rest in order to recover from nearly two weeks of inadequate sleep and irregular meals. However, on August 14, despite still not feeling well, I had to travel to the Municipality of Ayungon at 7:00 AM to get my NBI clearance, which had been scheduled for that day. Even though I was not feeling well, I forced myself to travel because I did not want to miss the appointment.

Around 3:00 PM, I arrived back in San Carlos and was planning to get a medical certificate. However, I also had to assist my uncle with settling an issue regarding my BPI card. It was urgent because the money that needed to be withdrawn was intended as payment for my uncle's loan. Because of this, I went to BPI to settle the issue, withdrew the money, and then travelled to Valle Hermoso to pay off his loan.

I returned to San Carlos at around 6:30 PM. By that time, I had not had enough rest or a proper meal, and I was already extremely exhausted and experiencing a severe headache. I could no longer bear the tiredness, so I went to sleep.

At midnight on August 15, despite still not feeling well, I decided that I had to report to work. I was worried about my work statistics and also felt responsible for the additional workload and burden that my absence had caused my Team Leader. I went to work for my scheduled shift even though I did not have a medical certificate. 

I sincerely apologize for not being able to provide a medical certificate. I did try to obtain one on Saturday by looking for a private doctor who could assess my condition and issue the necessary documentation. However, I was declined by three doctors because it was Saturday and their offices were closed.

I sincerely acknowledge that I should have handled the situation better, and I apologize for the inconvenience and additional workload my absence may have caused my Team Leader and the team. I understand the importance of being present and responsible for my attendance, and I take full responsibility for failing to report to work on August 12 and August 14 . My intention was never to disregard my responsibilities, but at that time, I was struggling physically due to prolonged lack of sleep, inadequate rest, and irregular meals. I am truly sorry for what happened, and I will do my best to prevent a similar situation from happening again.
Employee Commitment:
I acknowledge the corrective action issued to me regarding my two instances of absence without providing the required medical certificate. I understand the importance of following the company’s attendance and documentation policies, and I sincerely apologize for my failure to comply with the required procedure. I acknowledge the verbal warning given to me and take this matter seriously. Moving forward, I commit to improving my attendance and ensuring that I properly communicate any absence to my immediate supervisor/management within the required timeframe. In cases where a medical certificate or other supporting document is required, I will make sure to provide the necessary documentation in accordance with company policy. I understand that compliance with attendance policies is part of my responsibility as an employee. I will take the necessary steps to prevent this from happening again and will be more mindful of the proper procedures whenever I am unable to report for work.

Thank you for giving me the opportunity to acknowledge this matter and demonstrate my commitment to improvement.

COCD Provision on Attendance: Section 1.24 – Incurring at least one (1) tardiness notice within sixty (60) days from the issuance of a First Written Warning for violation of the Attendance Guideline.

Rose Sheen Vergara incurred three (3) consecutive recorded instances of tardiness this month:

• August 12, 2026: 21 minutes late
• August 13, 2026: 18 minutes late

Reason: Transportation difficulties from Calatrava.

Discussion / Corrective Action:

As a corrective action, Sheen was instructed to make proactive transportation arrangements, allow sufficient travel time, and establish a contingency plan to minimize the risk of further tardiness. She was also reminded that continued attendance violations may result in further corrective action in accordance with company policy.

Description:
On August 16, 2026, Dominic was absent from work and cited body pain as the reason for his absence. He was advised to provide a valid medical certificate (medcert) to support and validate his illness-related absence. However, upon his return to work, Dominic failed to submit the required medical certificate within the prescribed 24-hour period.

The failure to provide the required medical documentation resulted in the absence being treated as an unauthorized absence, in accordance with COCD Policy 1.22, which covers incurring one (1) unauthorized absence due to reasons other than being sick and/or being unable to present a valid medical certificate from an HMO-accredited doctor within 24 hours upon return to work.

Dominic was reminded that a valid medical certificate must contain the necessary details for verification, including the doctor’s name and signature, PRC license number, clinic address, and clinic phone number, and must be issued by an HMO-accredited doctor.

This is Dominic’s first instance of this infraction. As a corrective action, a Verbal Warning is being issued to formally address the infraction and reinforce the importance of complying with the company’s attendance and documentation requirements. Dominic is expected to submit complete and valid supporting documentation within the prescribed timeline for any future illness-related absences and to ensure full compliance with COCD Policy 1.22 moving forward. Any recurrence may result in further corrective action in accordance with company policy.
Employee Explanation:
Dear Sir/Maam,
I respectfully submit this written response regarding the Notice to Explain issued to me concerning my absence from work on August 16, 2026 and my failure to submit the required medical certificate within the prescribed 24-hour period.

I acknowledge that I was absent from work on the stated date due to illness. At the time, I was experiencing symptoms that made me unable to report for work. I informed the appropriate person regarding my absence and cited my illness as the reason.

Regarding the medical certificate, I understand and acknowledge the company's requirement to submit valid medical documentation within the prescribed period. Description:
Andross Sevilla committed  a call avoidance it was identified during a call audit conducted on August 18, 2026. The incident falls under Group III – Provisions on Quality, Section 3.9 – Call Avoidance, under the Company’s Code of Conduct and Discipline (COCD).

Under the Company’s COCD, Call Avoidance under Group III, Section 3.9 is classified as a terminable offense even for a first offense. Accordingly, this incident is subject to the corresponding disciplinary action in accordance with Company policy.

Incident Details

Incident 1
Date: August 18, 2026
Time: 4:26:55 PM PHT
Interaction ID: 91834063

The interaction was an order placement. The agent provided the opening spiel while the customer was speaking and selecting an item. At approximately 00:39, the agent disconnected the call by clicking the “X” button in Jabber, despite the customer interaction still being in progress.

Incident 2
Date: August 14, 2026
Time: 2:42:33 PM PHT
Interaction ID: 91789334

The customer contacted the company to place an order and requested to update the credit card. The agent proceeded to ask about the item. At approximately 01:08, the agent disconnected the call by clicking the “X” button in Jabber while the customer interaction was still ongoing.

Incident 3
Date: August 14, 2026
Time: 2:31:54 PM PHT
Interaction ID: 91789129

The agent was present at her workstation, and mouse movement was observed; however, there was no verbal response from the agent during the interaction. At approximately 01:09, the agent disconnected the call by clicking the “X” button in Jabber.

Additional Call Audit Findings

During the same audit, additional interactions were identified where the agent appeared to be unresponsive or inattentive. These interactions are being documented separately for review, as they did not clearly establish that the agent manually disconnected the call:

August 13, 2026 – 2:13:09 PM PHT | Interaction ID: 91777288: The agent appeared inattentive. Mouse movement was observed, but there was no verbal response from the agent. Background audio was also captured.
August 16, 2026 – 2:53:35 PM PHT | Interaction ID: 91810767: The agent did not respond to the customer. Mouse movement was observed, but there was no verbal response.
August 16, 2026 | Interaction ID: 91810228: The agent initially provided the opening spiel. However, when the customer raised a concern, the agent became silent. The customer repeatedly said “hello,” but the agent did not respond, eventually resulting in the call being disconnected.

No system issue was reported for the interactions where the agent remained on her workstation but did not respond to the customer.

Coaching and Agent Acknowledgment

Andross was coached regarding the identified call avoidance incidents. During the coaching discussion, she acknowledged and admitted that she disconnected the confirmed calls by clicking the “X” button in Jabber. She explained that she committed the behavior because she was very sleepy at the time.

Andross also acknowledged that she was already aware of the Company’s call avoidance policy, as the policy and expected call-handling procedures were discussed during her onboarding. The seriousness of the violation was reiterated during the coaching session.

She was reminded that being tired or sleepy does not justify intentionally disconnecting a customer interaction. She was expected to follow the proper call-handling process and use the appropriate support or break procedures when experiencing fatigue.

Policy Violation and Disciplinary Consequence

The confirmed incidents constitute Call Avoidance and fall under Group III – Provisions on Quality, Section 3.9 – Call Avoidance of the Company’s Code of Conduct and Discipline (COCD).

This violation is classified as a terminable offense even for a first offense under the applicable COCD provision. Andross was informed of the seriousness of the violation and that the incident may result in termination of employment in accordance with the Company’s policy and due process requirements.

Andross acknowledged the discussion and admitted responsibility for the confirmed call avoidance incidents. She was reminded of the importance of strict compliance with the Company’s policies and proper call-handling procedures .
Employee Explanation:
I am writing to explain the incident regarding the calls that I intentionally disconnected during my shift.

I sincerely apologize for my actions. At that time, I was extremely sleepy and had difficulty maintaining my alertness and focus. Instead of handling the situation properly, I made the wrong decision to disconnect the calls. I understand that this was not an appropriate action and that it may have affected our customers, the team, and our service quality.

I take full responsibility for my mistake and understand that being sleepy is not an excuse for intentionally disconnecting customer calls. Moving forward, I will make sure to manage my rest and personal circumstances properly so I can remain alert and perform my responsibilities effectively.

I sincerely apologize for the incident and assure you that I will learn from this mistake and avoid repeating it in the future.

Thank you for your understanding.

Description:
Juren was previously instructed to promptly inform me of all important matters concerning the AiFi account, particularly tricky sessions included in the Global Audits that require either my or AM Connie's review and decision, as well as important process updates that may impact operations if not properly communicated and cascaded.

However, Juren failed to inform me of a recent AiFi error that was initially tagged incorrectly. The issue required re-evaluation and was subsequently confirmed and declared as an error by the client. Timely escalation of such cases is important to ensure that appropriate guidance and action can be provided before the matter progresses further.

Additionally, Juren failed to cascade an important update in the DAT Guide concerning a change in the process for handling sessions where a customer enters the store with an item, places it in a triggerable location, and subsequently picks it up again. The updated process was not communicated to Operations, which resulted in an operator error. The update was only identified when the Team Lead investigated the matter and reviewed the DAT Guide, where the process change was found. The Team Lead then cascaded the information to the Operations team.

When asked about the lack of cascading, Juren explained that he assumed the Operations team was already aware of the update. However, given his responsibility to monitor and communicate important process changes, this assumption resulted in the information not being properly cascaded to the affected team.

These incidents demonstrate a lapse in the proper execution of his responsibilities, particularly in monitoring important account updates, escalating matters that require management or client review, and ensuring that relevant process changes are properly communicated to Operations. The failure to perform these responsibilities resulted in an avoidable client-confirmed error and an operational error that could have been prevented through timely escalation, verification, and proper cascading of information.
Employee Explanation:
I acknowledge the concern regarding my failure to escalate the session after identifying red flags during my review. I sincerely apologize for overlooking the item carried by the shopper and for not seeking additional guidance before finalizing the audit.

At the time of the review, the session presented a complex camera angle with limited visibility, and the shopper's pickup of the item was not clearly visible. The session had also been processed by an operator who was being assisted by a Team Lead, which initially gave me additional confidence that the annotation had been reviewed appropriately. During my own audit, I identified red flags and attempted to validate the session based on the available camera view. However, because the pickup event itself was not clearly captured, I ultimately classified the issue under camera visibility rather than escalating it for further review.

I recognize that this was my judgment error. I should have escalated the session to AM Connie or sought another level of validation instead of making the final determination based solely on my interpretation of the camera angle. I understand that as QA, particularly when a session contains ambiguity or potential client-impacting errors, it is important to seek clarification rather than rely on assumptions.

My decision was also influenced by a previous experience where I had sought validation on a session and was advised that the session was acceptable, but the same session was later identified by the client as a deviation. That experience made me more cautious about requesting another review and contributed to my decision to make the determination myself. However, I understand that this does not excuse my failure to escalate the current case.

I sincerely apologize for this lapse and take accountability for my decision. My intention was never to conceal or disregard an AiFi error. I was attempting to make the best judgment based on the available camera evidence, but I recognize that the appropriate action in a complex and uncertain case should have been escalation.

Moving forward, I will apply a stricter escalation approach for sessions involving unclear camera angles, questionable item attribution, or any red flag that cannot be conclusively validated. I will also seek a second-level review when necessary rather than relying solely on my own judgment. This experience has reinforced the importance of timely escalation and has given me a clear area for improvement in my QA responsibilities.

Regarding the concern about the failure to cascade the updated DAT Guide process, I would like to clarify the timeline and circumstances surrounding this matter.

At the time when the process update was originally cascaded by Daniel, I was not yet functioning as the QA Lead responsible for overseeing the overall QA-to-Operations cascade. My responsibilities at that point were primarily focused on supporting QA activities, particularly session auditing and other assigned QA tasks following the calibration.

Based on my understanding of the timeline, the process update was introduced before I assumed responsibility for the QA Lead function. Because the update was not part of the information that I personally received as the responsible QA Lead at that time, I was not aware that this particular change had not been properly cascaded to Operations.

When the issue was later identified through the Team Lead's investigation of the DAT Guide, I understood that the information had not reached the affected Operations team. I acknowledge that, once I became responsible for QA leadership and process monitoring, I should have verified that important process updates were properly communicated and understood by Operations. However, I respectfully believe it is important to distinguish between a process communication gap that occurred before I assumed the relevant responsibility and a failure to perform an obligation that was already under my direct ownership.

I also want to clarify that I have consistently supported Operations whenever process concerns, audit findings, or guidance were brought to my attention. I have conducted audits, assisted operators, supported calibrations, provided guidance, and worked with Operations to address quality concerns. I have never intentionally withheld an important process update or refused to support the Operations team.

I sincerely regret that the process update was not properly cascaded and that this eventually contributed to an operator error. However, I respectfully ask that the timeline of responsibilities be considered when evaluating my accountability for this incident. I should not be held solely responsible for a communication gap that originated before I assumed the QA Lead responsibility, particularly when I was not aware at the time that the update had not reached Operations.

Moving forward, I will ensure that all important client process changes, DAT Guide revisions, and calibration decisions are actively tracked and formally cascaded to the appropriate Operations stakeholders
Employee Commitment:
Moving forward, I am committed to strengthening my accountability, judgment, communication, and proactiveness in the performance of my QA responsibilities.

For audit-related concerns, I will no longer rely solely on my own interpretation when a session has complex camera angles, unclear item attribution, or other red flags that cannot be conclusively validated. I will proactively seek a second-level review or escalate the session to the appropriate QA or Operations leadership before finalizing the audit. This will help ensure that uncertain cases are properly evaluated and that potential client-impacting errors are addressed in a timely manner.

For process and policy updates, I will also take a more proactive approach in monitoring client calibrations, DAT Guide revisions, and other process changes. I will maintain a clear record of important updates, verify whether they have been properly communicated to Operations, and ensure that affected Team Leads and operators receive the necessary guidance. Rather than assuming that an update has already been cascaded, I will personally verify and document the communication whenever the responsibility falls within my scope.

I also commit to improving my communication whenever there is uncertainty regarding ownership, task priorities, or process changes. If I am unsure whether a responsibility has already been handled or whether an instruction applies to me, I will seek clarification rather than make an assumption.

I recognize that these incidents have highlighted areas where I can improve, particularly in timely escalation, proactive communication, and verification of process updates. I sincerely regret the lapses that occurred and take these experiences as an opportunity to strengthen my performance as a QA professional and leader.

I remain committed to maintaining the quality standards expected of me, supporting Operations, protecting the accuracy of our audits, and ensuring that client requirements are properly understood and implemented. Description:

This resulted in the item being incorrectly added during subsequent session processing.

The root cause was a process-adherence gap, as the operator did not consistently apply the required validation process to thoroughly identify and account for all carried items at the start of the session.

This corrective action serves as a VERBAL WARNING. The operator acknowledged the feedback and committed to exercising greater caution, consistently following the required process, and preventing similar errors from recurring.

During the entrance check, I was unable to fully identify and validate all of the items already in the shopper’s possession. Although the missed event was eventually identified and the edge case was processed accordingly, the item in question had already been overlooked during the initial validation. As a result, it was later incorrectly counted as an additional item, which led to the Quantity Too Much error.

I understand that the entrance check is a critical part of the process because it establishes the correct baseline of the items that the shopper is already carrying before the session proceeds. In this instance, I acknowledge that I did not apply the required validation process as thoroughly and carefully as I should have. While the error was unintentional, I recognize that it could have been prevented if I had taken additional time to carefully inspect, identify, and confirm all items in the shopper’s possession during the entrance check.

I sincerely apologize for this oversight and acknowledge the impact that process deviations can have on session accuracy and overall operations. I understand that even a single missed item during the entrance validation can affect the accuracy of the succeeding session events. This incident has reinforced the importance of consistently following the established process and not relying solely on assumptions or an incomplete visual assessment.

Moving forward, I will be more deliberate and attentive during every entrance validation. I will thoroughly inspect and account for all items already being carried by the shopper before proceeding with the succeeding cases. I will also avoid rushing the validation process and will perform an additional review whenever there is uncertainty regarding an item or event. By doing so, I can ensure that the correct baseline is established before continuing with the session and reduce the possibility of similar errors occurring.

I acknowledge the corrective action and the verbal warning issued in connection with this incident. I appreciate the feedback provided and the opportunity to address the identified process gap. I take full responsibility for my part in the incident and will use this experience as an opportunity to improve my attention to detail, strengthen my adherence to the required procedures, and apply greater care during entrance validation.

I am committed to making the necessary improvements and taking the appropriate precautions to prevent a similar error from occurring again.

Thank you for the opportunity to explain and address this matter.

Description:
Juren was instructed to prioritize auditing the Pre-DAT sessions of the new hires to monitor their performance and ensure that any gaps or concerns were identified and addressed early. He was specifically instructed to prioritize these audits on Monday and was not scheduled to facilitate training that day to allow sufficient time to complete the assigned audits.

Despite this, Juren was unable to complete the required Pre-DAT audits. He explained that he did not have sufficient time because he was also transferring or pasting the audit results into the Global Audits sheet. However, this additional task should not have prevented him from completing the assigned audits, as transferring the results to the Global Audits sheet only requires a short amount of time. The priority given to the Pre-DAT audits was intended to ensure that the performance of the new hires was properly monitored, particularly during their initial training period.

There were also concerns regarding the proper facilitation and management of the new-hire training. On two consecutive days, the new hires were scheduled to report at 8:00 PM, while Juren's scheduled start time was 9:00 PM, resulting in the new hires being left without their designated trainer for approximately one hour. As the designated trainer and the person who endorsed the trainees to the client, Juren is expected to take ownership of the trainees' development, monitor their progress, and ensure that they are properly supported throughout their scheduled training activities.

Instead, Juren requested to adjust his shift to match the new hires' schedule. While the request itself may be addressed through proper scheduling coordination, the concern is that the one-hour training coverage gap had already occurred on two consecutive days without proactive action to ensure that the new hires were properly supported. This is particularly concerning given that Juren has previously handled new-hire training and is expected to understand and anticipate the requirements associated with the trainer role.

These instances demonstrate a need for greater ownership, initiative, and accountability in carrying out his responsibilities as a QA and trainer. Juren is expected to properly prioritize assigned tasks, manage his time effectively, proactively identify and address gaps in training coverage, and take ownership of the performance and development of the new hires under his supervision. Going forward, he is expected to demonstrate greater proactiveness and ensure that assigned responsibilities are completed without requiring repeated direction or intervention from Management.
Employee Explanation:
I respectfully acknowledge the concerns raised regarding the completion of the Pre-DAT audits and the training coverage of the new hires. I would like to provide the following explanation and context regarding the circumstances surrounding these instances.

I understand that the Pre-DAT audits were intended to be prioritized on Monday to ensure that the performance of the new hires could be monitored early and that any gaps could be identified and addressed. I acknowledge that I was not able to complete all of the required Pre-DAT audits within that period, and I sincerely regret that this expectation was not fully met.

However, I would like to clarify the workload and circumstances I was managing on that day.

On Monday, I was assigned approximately 127 sessions for audit. The sessions also contained lengthy and complex cases that required careful review. At that time, I was primarily handling the audit workload myself, although one of the Team Leads was also reviewing some sessions. Despite the assistance, I still needed to personally double-check the sessions to ensure the accuracy and quality of my audits and to minimize the possibility of a deviation from the client's evaluation.

While completing these audits, I was also providing support to Operations. There were instances where operators and Team Leads sought confirmation regarding specific sessions, particularly cases involving product identification and quantity determination. Although QA had been advised to focus on QA-related tasks on Monday, there were still Team Leads present who were supporting Operations, and I was nevertheless approached for confirmation on certain cases.

Once assistance was provided on one case, similar inquiries from other operators followed, particularly concerning product and quantity validation. As part of my QA responsibilities, I did not simply disregard these concerns when operators were seeking clarification because providing guidance and helping prevent potential errors is also part of my role. These support requests consequently consumed time that could otherwise have been allocated to the remaining Pre-DAT audits.

Additionally, at around the 1:00 AM shift, one of the Team Leads encountered difficulty assisting the operators. I took the initiative to provide support to help prevent additional errors from occurring. My intention in doing so was to protect the quality of Operations and prevent avoidable issues, rather than to deprioritize the Pre-DAT audits.

I also had the responsibility of transferring and updating audit results in the Global Audits sheet. I understand that this task by itself does not require a significant amount of time. My point is not that the transfer itself prevented me from completing the Pre-DAT audits, but rather that it was one of several responsibilities being handled alongside the primary audit workload, operator support, and session validation.

I recognize that I should have communicated earlier that the volume and complexity of the Monday audit workload, together with the additional support requests, were affecting my ability to complete the Pre-DAT audits within the expected timeframe. I take accountability for not proactively raising this concern and requesting prioritization or additional support when I recognized that the workload could affect the completion of the assigned Pre-DAT audits.

I would like to emphasize, however, that the incomplete Pre-DAT audits were not the result of neglecting the responsibility or intentionally disregarding management's instruction. I was actively performing QA duties throughout the shift, including auditing, validating cases, supporting Operations, and taking initiative when additional support was needed.

Regarding the concern that the new hires were scheduled at 8:00 PM while my scheduled start time was 9:00 PM, I would like to clarify that I followed the schedule and working arrangement that had previously been assigned and followed by the QA team.

At the time, I was not given a specific instruction that I was required to change my schedule or mirror the trainees' 8:00 PM schedule. My understanding was that the new hires' upskilling/training program would run for approximately one month, while my existing work schedule remained in place. My supervisor was also aware of my existing schedule, and there had been no prior instruction during the preceding days requiring me to change my start time specifically to match the trainees.

This was particularly important from my perspective because I had previously been reminded regarding the importance of aligning my attendance with operational requirements, including concerns about clocking in without mirroring the Operations schedule. Therefore, I continued following my established schedule while also ensuring that I remained available to support Operations and perform my QA responsibilities.

I acknowledge that, in hindsight, I should have proactively clarified whether the new-hire training schedule required me to formally adjust my shift and should have raised the potential one-hour coverage gap as soon as I became aware of it. I accept that this would have demonstrated greater initiative and would have prevented the misunderstanding.

However, I respectfully clarify that the schedule was not intentionally disregarded. I was operating based on the schedule and instructions available to me at the time, and I was not informed that I was expected to mirror the trainees' schedule.

When I recognized the scheduling concern, I requested an adjustment so that my working hours could align with the trainees' schedule and ensure that I could provide appropriate training coverage. My intention was to resolve the issue and ensure that the trainees received the necessary support.

I understand the importance of ownership, initiative, and accountability in my role as QA and trainer. I also recognize that, regardless of the number of competing responsibilities, I need to communicate potential conflicts early rather than allow them to affect the completion of a priority assignment.

Moving forward, I will take the following actions:

Prioritize explicitly assigned critical tasks and establish a clear completion plan at the beginning of the shift.
Immediately communicate to Management when workload, support requests, or competing assignments may affect a priority deliverable.
Clarify training schedules and coverage requirements in advance rather than relying on previous scheduling practices.
Maintain clear documentation of assigned QA and training responsibilities and their respective deadlines.
Continue providing appropriate support to Operations while ensuring that such support does not compromise explicitly prioritized QA deliverables.
Proactively confirm expectations whenever there is uncertainty regarding scheduling, training coverage, or task priority.

I sincerely apologize for the gaps identified in these instances. I accept the areas where I could have demonstrated better communication and prioritization. At the same time, I respectfully ask that the circumstances, workload, existing instructions, and the fact that I continued performing my QA and Operations support responsibilities be considered in evaluating these incidents.

My intention throughout these situations was to fulfill my responsibilities, maintain audit quality, support Operations, and prevent additional errors. I remain committed to improving my prioritization, communication, and proactive coordination so that similar concerns do not occur again.

Description:
Hi Team,

This Incident Report is being raised to request corrective action regarding agent John Ron Pelotinia for being away from his station without authorization for an extended period.
